summary:
Marswalk Planner is a web app that lets astronauts plan and rehearse a walk on Mars before they leave the habitat. It shows a 2 × 2 km area of Mount Sharp in Gale crater as a 3D map and combines seven NASA data sources on it: high-resolution images, elevation, night-time temperature, minerals, the Curiosity rover's track and photos, weather, and radiation.

The app finds the fastest safe route on foot between science stops and checks it against suit endurance, walk-back time, daylight and radiation dose, ending in a clear GO or NO-GO. The crew can fly the route, see it from inside the helmet, practise a solar-storm abort, and print the plan as a wrist checklist.

It matters because a Marswalk has a hard time limit and no rescue. The data to plan one safely already exists, but it is scattered across archives built for scientists. Marswalk Planner turns it into one picture a crew can act on.
details:
What is creative about it

Most Mars maps answer "what is there?". Marswalk Planner answers "can I go there and still get home?". Every cell of the map knows how long the walk back to the habitat takes, so safety is computed for the whole area, not only along one line. Each science stop is a place the Curiosity rover really stood, which gives the crew a ground photo of their destination before they leave. And the plan leaves the screen: it prints as a wrist checklist, as Apollo crews used on the Moon.

What we considered

We built the tool around the limits of a person in a suit: slope and step height they can manage, walking speed, hours of consumables, an untouchable reserve, daylight, and radiation dose. We decided to state every assumption openly and make it adjustable, and to mark where the data is weak, for example the faint mineral signals. The app has no build step and needs no connection once loaded, because a tool for Mars cannot depend on a server on Earth.
